courses.title: Discrete Math I
courses.prerequisiteText: BC Pre-Calculus 12 or BC Calculus 12 (or equivalent), or any of MATH 100, 150, 151, 154, 157.
courses.description: Introduction to graph theory, trees, induction, automata theory, formal reasoning, modular arithmetic.

courses.prerequisiteText: MATH 141 or MACM 101 or (ENSC 251 and one of MATH 232 or MATH 240).

courses.title: Computing with Linear Algebra
courses.prerequisiteText: One of CMPT 102, 120, 126, 128 or 130 and one of MATH 150, 151, 154 or 157 and one of MATH 232 or 240.
courses.description: Using a mathematical software package for doing calculations in linear algebra. Development of computer models that analyze and illustrate applications of linear algebra. All calculations and experiments will be done in the Matlab software package. Topics include: large-scale matrix calculations, experiments with cellular automata, indexing, searching and ranking pages on the internet, population models, data fitting and optimization, image analysis, and cryptography.

courses.title: Intro to Computer Algebra
courses.prerequisiteText: CMPT 307 or ((MATH 340 or MATH 342) and (CMPT 225 or MACM 204)).
courses.description: Data structures and algorithms for mathematical objects. Topics include long integer arithmetic, computing polynomial greatest common divisors, the fast Fourier transform, Hensel's lemma and p-adic methods, differentiation and simplification of formulae, and polynomial factorization. Students will use a computer algebra system such as Maple for calculations and programming.

courses.title: Quantum Algorithms
courses.prerequisiteText: MATH 232 or MATH 240, with a minimum grade of C-.
courses.description: An introductory treatment of quantum computing with an emphasis on quantum algorithms. Topics include the gate model of quantum computation focusing on the design and implementation of quantum algorithms. Basic knowledge of algorithms and complexity will be an asset, but not required. No prior knowledge of physics or quantum mechanics is necessary, only a solid background in linear algebra.
